title: UK Biobank adds immune and brain health layers - Nature Biotechnology
gist: UK Biobank is adding a population-scale immune dataset (with IMU Biosciences, 80,000 participants) and a neurodegeneration proteomics study (Alamar Biosciences, 80,000 samples), with tools from Becton Dickinson, Waters and Ultima Genomics feeding an AI foundational dataset.

insights.claim: UK Biobank and IMU Biosciences, backed by a £1.57 million ($2.10 million) grant from Sovereign AI, will build a population-scale immune dataset from blood samples of 80,000 participants using immune-cell profiling, transcriptomics and AI methods.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Population-scale immune data becomes a training asset for AI drug discovery; UK sovereign AI funding is flowing into biology datasets.
insights.locator: The collaboration with London-based IMU Biosciences

insights.claim: The UK Biobank immune project expects to generate over 100 million data points per 2-ml blood sample, profiling around 2,500 immune cell subsets for a single-cell immune AI foundational dataset.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Data density of this scale is aimed at foundation-model training, signalling where biological AI data generation is heading.
insights.quote: The immune project expects to generate over 100 million data points from each 2-ml blood sample
insights.locator: The immune project expects to generate

insights.claim: The UK Biobank immune study will use Becton Dickinson flow cytometry, Waters single-cell multi-omics instruments and Ultima Genomics sequencers alongside IMU's platform.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Large biobank projects are reference wins for tools vendors; Ultima's inclusion signals traction as an alternative sequencing supplier.
insights.locator: The study will apply IMU’s immune profiling platform

insights.claim: UK Biobank will analyze 80,000 samples with Alamar Biosciences' proteomics platform, funded by Alzheimer's Research UK and LifeArc, to find low-abundance protein signals that may predict Alzheimer's and Parkinson's decades before symptoms.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Early-detection blood biomarkers for neurodegeneration are a growing diagnostics market; high-sensitivity proteomics vendors benefit.
insights.locator: And in October, the UK Biobank announced

insights.claim: Data from the UK Biobank immune and proteomics expansions will be made available to approved researchers worldwide, extending the biobank's role as a shared resource for drug discovery.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open access to these layers lowers data costs for AI-biotech startups and pharma target discovery.
insights.locator: The resulting data will be added to the UK Biobank
